ref_clues.ref_content: The rx_break_err interrupt is triggered if a break condition has been detected. A break condition is defined as the RX pin being continuously low for more than a programmable number of character-times (via CTRL.RXBLVL, either 2, 4, 8, or 16). The current break status can be read from STATUS.BREAK. If STATUS.BREAK is set but INTR_STATE.BREAK is clear then the line break is still going on but interrupt has been cleared. If STATUS.BREAK is clear but INTR_STATE.BREAK is set then there has been a line break for which software has not cleared the interrupt but the line is now back to normal. Frame errors will continue to be reported after a break error.

ref_clues.ref_content: The rx_break_err interrupt is triggered if a break condition has been detected. A break condition is defined as the RX pin being continuously low for more than a programmable number of character-times (via CTRL.RXBLVL, either 2, 4, 8, or 16). Only one interrupt is generated per break -- the line must return high for at least half a bit-time before an additional break interrupt is generated. The current break status can be read from STATUS.BREAK. If STATUS.BREAK is set but INTR_STATE.BREAK is clear then the line break is still going on but interrupt has been cleared. If STATUS.BREAK is clear but INTR_STATE.BREAK is set then there has been a line break for which software has not cleared the interrupt but the line is now back to normal. Frame errors will continue to be reported after a break error.
Inject frame error in parity and non-parity cases by not setting stop bit = 1. Ensure the interrupt gets asserted.

ref_clues.ref_content: Register FIFO_CTRL [rw]: UART FIFO control. Fields: RXRST (bit0 write 1 resets RX FIFO, read returns 0), TXRST (bit1 write 1 resets TX FIFO, read returns 0), RXILVL (bits4:2 trigger level for RX interrupts: if FIFO depth >= setting, raises rx_watermark; values 0=1,1=2,2=4,3=8,4=16,5=32,6=62 characters), TXILVL (bits7:5 trigger level for TX interrupts: if FIFO depth < setting, raises tx_watermark; values 0=1,1=2,2=4,3=8,4=16 characters).

If the RX FIFO level becomes greater than or equal to RX water mark level (configurable via FIFO_CTRL.RXILVL), the rx_watermark interrupt is raised. The watermark interrupts are level-based: they stay asserted as long as the FIFO levels violate the configured level and cannot be cleared by writing to the status register.
